prompts.LoanAmount: Check that the amount fits the purpose and the applicant's income.
prompts.Purpose: Ask what the money is for in detail and whether it can be documented.
prompts.EmploymentLength: Confirm the employer and how long the applicant has worked there.
prompts.HomeOwnership: Confirm the housing situation and the monthly housing cost.
prompts.AnnualIncome: Verify the income with pay slips or a tax return.
prompts.IncomeVerification: Get documents that confirm the stated income.
prompts.DebtToIncomePercent: List the existing monthly debt payments and check them against the credit report.
prompts.CreditScore: Read the credit report behind the score, not only the number.
prompts.EarliestCreditLine: A short credit history gives the model little to go on; look for other evidence of repayment.
prompts.InquiriesLast6Months: Ask what new credit the applicant applied for recently and whether it was granted.
prompts.DelinquenciesLast2Years: Ask about the late payments and whether they are settled.
prompts.PublicRecords: Look up each public record and whether it is settled.
prompts.Bankruptcies: Check when the bankruptcy was and whether it is discharged.
prompts.RevolvingBalance: Check the card balances and whether this loan pays them down.
prompts.RevolvingUtilizationPercent: Ask why the cards are close to their limits and whether this loan pays them down.
prompts.OpenAccounts: Review the open credit lines on the credit report.
prompts.TotalAccounts: Review the account history on the credit report.
prompts.MortgageAccounts: Confirm the mortgage payments and include them in the monthly budget.

models.title: Model
models.intro: What the scoring model is, what its number means, and where it should not be trusted.
models.noActive: No model is set as active, so new applications are recorded without a score.
models.whyCost1: In the training loans, a loan that defaulted lost on average $4,203.69, and a loan paid back in full earned on average $2,057.47. A missed default therefore costs about 2.04 times as much as turning away a good borrower.
models.whyCost2: Rejecting is cheaper on average once P(bad) reaches 1 / (1 + 2.0431), about 32.9%. Below that, approving is cheaper.
models.whyCost3: The amounts are what borrowers paid back minus what was lent, from Lending Club's records. They leave out funding cost and the time value of money.
models.whyFixed: This threshold was recommended with the model and fixed when it was registered. A different threshold means registering the model again.
models.whyRangesValue: They follow Lending Club's loans of that period; extreme values are capped inside the model
models.registryNote: Shadow models score every new application next to the active one. Only the active model makes the recommendation, and officers do not see shadow scores.
models.availableNote: A model starts as a shadow. Its threshold and review band are the ones it was trained with and cannot be changed afterwards.
models.availableError: The inference service could not list its models
models.availableErrorText: Registered models are unaffected. Try again once the service is running.
models.nothingNewText: Every model the inference service serves is already in the registry.
models.logEmptyText: Registrations and role changes appear here with who made them and why.
models.limit1: The model learned from loans Lending Club granted. It never saw how the applicants it turned away would have repaid, so its estimates are least reliable for applicants unlike those it approved.
models.limit2: The loans are US loans issued from 2012 to 2014. Tested once on loans from 2015, it predicted somewhat fewer defaults than occurred.
models.limit3: Longer terms were left out, so the form offers no other term.
models.limit4Title: The review band is not a safeguard by itself.
models.limit4: It marks the applications where the model is least sure. It lowers losses only if the officer's closer look judges those cases better than the model does.
models.limit5: Every application needs the officer's decision, with a reason when it goes against the model, when the model asks for a closer review, or when no score was available.
models.limit6: are kept in the experiment log and are not shown on this page.
